draft.title: Grid references, latitude and longitude
card: Area reference
a four-figure code that names one grid square on a map. Read the eastings (the vertical lines, numbered left to right) first, then the northings (the horizontal lines, numbered bottom to top).
Grid reference

a six-figure code that pins down a point inside a square. Each half has three digits: the eastings first, then the northings. The first two digits of each half are the line number, and the third is tenths of the way to the next line.
Latitude
measures how far a place is north or south of the equator, in degrees. The equator is 0°, and the poles are 90° N and 90° S.
Longitude

measures how far a place is east or west of the prime meridian, in degrees. The prime meridian is 0° and runs through Greenwich in London. Latitude is given first, then longitude: Melbourne is about 38° S, 145° E.
draft.remember: Grid references give eastings then northings. Latitude and longitude give degrees north or south, then east or west.

a.q: A map reference is written as 4 5 (eastings 4, northings 5). Which way should a student read it to find the square?
opts: Along to line 4, then up to line 5
Up to line 5, then along to line 4
Along to line 5, then up to line 4
Down from line 4, then back to line 5
a.why: Eastings come first, so the student goes along the bottom to line 4, then up to line 5. Reading up first reverses the order, which is a common mistake.

b.q: Tess reads that a lighthouse is at 34° S, 151° E. Where is it on Earth?
opts: South of the equator and east of the prime meridian
North of the equator and east of the prime meridian
South of the equator and west of the prime meridian
North of the equator and west of the prime meridian
b.why: S means south of the equator, and E means east of the prime meridian. The first number is latitude and the second is longitude, so 34° S is the latitude and 151° E is the longitude.
b.clue: S and E tell you the direction from the equator and the prime meridian.

wants.brief: A simple map grid with vertical eastings lines numbered left to right and horizontal northings lines numbered bottom to top. One grid square is shaded and labelled as an area reference. A dot inside a square shows a point, with the eastings digits and northings digits marked beside it.
wants.why: It shows how eastings come before northings and how the third digit locates a point inside a square.

wants.brief: A globe or world map with the equator marked as 0° latitude, the prime meridian marked as 0° longitude, and lines of latitude labelled north and south and lines of longitude labelled east and west.
wants.why: It lets a student see which lines measure latitude and which measure longitude.

a.best: Along to line 4, then up to line 5

b.best: South of the equator and east of the prime meridian

a.q: Jai is given the area reference 4552 on a topographic map. Which two grid lines meet at the bottom-left corner of that square?
opts: Easting 45 and northing 52
Easting 52 and northing 45
Easting 46 and northing 53
Easting 44 and northing 51
a.why: Eastings come first, so the first two digits, 45, are the easting and the last two, 52, are the northing. The square is named by the lines at its bottom-left corner. Swapping them to easting 52 and northing 45 reverses the order, which is a common mistake.
a.clue: Which half of the code is the easting?
